Codebase: `ProviderSession.__init__` registers `openai` builder ONLY when `cfg.base_url` is set; `anthropic` and `bedrock` are always registered — but the plan never says 'registered rebar builder without base_url = first_class'
findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel `tier` field with values `first_class` / `best_effort` but never specifies the classification rule — which provider configurations map to each value. The Testing section implies `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL` → `best_effort` and `bedrock` → `first_class`, but the decision algorithm is not stated: it is unclear whether the rule is 'registered rebar builder without base_url → first_class', 'base_url set → best_effort regardless of provider', or something based on the `ProviderSession` builder registry. This matters because the field is *signed and persisted* — a misclassification produces a non-correctable audit record, and an implementer who guesses wrong (e.g. treating the OpenAI-compatible S4 path under a hosted URL as `first_class`) cannot be caught by the specified tests, which only check Bedrock and `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL`.
findings.location: Approach section — `tier` field definition; Scope — `providers.py` entry; Testing — best-effort path
scenarios: An operator uses `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.anthropic.com/v1` (a real first-class endpoint hosted behind a proxy): the plan's `base_url` heuristic classifies this as `best_effort`, but semantically it is first-class — the signed provenance record would be permanently wrong.

An implementer interprets 'first_class = registered rebar builder' and classifies the S4 OpenAI path (which IS a registered rebar builder when base_url is set) as `first_class`, contradicting the testing section's intent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach section: '`tier` is `best_effort` when `cfg.base_url` is set (an opaque gateway whose backend tier is unknown), and `first_class` when the provider is a natively registered rebar builder (`anthropic` or `bedrock`) AND `cfg.base_url` is not set. The `openai` builder registered by S4 always implies `base_url` is set, so it is always `best_effort`.`

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the complete `tier` derivation rule as an explicit decision table (e.g., `bedrock` provider → `first_class`; direct `anthropic` provider → `first_class`; `openai` provider with `base_url` set → `best_effort`; pydantic-ai-delegated lazy-string providers → `best_effort` or `unknown`; `model_override`/fake runner → omit or `unknown`) co-located with the `provider_provenance` schema description.

Direct-Anthropic (non-Bedrock, no base_url) tier is never specified

ProviderSession._builders shows three registered providers (anthropic, bedrock, openai-via-base_url) plus pydantic-ai-delegated ones — the plan does not say which of these map to which tier
findings.finding: The `tier` derivation decision rule — the full logic mapping a provider configuration to `"first_class"` or `"best_effort"` — is only illustrated by two test examples (Bedrock → `first_class`, `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL` → `best_effort`) and never defined as a complete rule. Direct-Anthropic runs, lazy-string providers (openai/google), and the `model_override`/fake-runner path are all unaddressed. Since `tier` is part of a signed, non-repudiable verdict payload that consumers are explicitly invited to use for rejection decisions, the complete branching rule is load-bearing and its absence forces divergent implementer inference.
findings.location: Approach section — '`tier` is `first_class` or `best_effort`'; Testing section — 'happy path: a Bedrock run persists `tier == "first_class"`' and 'best-effort path: a run with `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL` persists `tier == "best_effort"`'
scenarios: An implementer assigns `first_class` to direct-Anthropic but another assigns `best_effort` to everything except Bedrock — producing silently divergent signed verdicts
A consumer filtering on `tier == "first_class"` rejects valid direct-Anthropic verdicts if the implementer mapped anthropic to `best_effort`
The fake/model_override path emits a `tier` value that wasn't intended to be consumable but ends up in a signed payload
findings.suggested_fix: Add a decision table to the Approach section, e.g.: `tier` is derived from `ProviderSession._builders`: a provider built by rebar's own registered builder for `anthropic` or `bedrock` is `first_class`; any `base_url`-backed `openai` builder or pydantic-ai-delegated provider is `best_effort`; the `model_override`/fake path omits `provider_provenance` or records `tier=null`.
